claims.title: Two attachment representations
claims.finding: Composer state separates inline attachments with extracted_content from file records with client identity, nativeFile, localPath, upload promise, abort control, server identity, and error state.

claims.title: Admission and model-aware file picker
claims.finding: Picker accept list depends on image support, out-of-context support, accept-all branches, and extension breakers. Count checks combine current attachments, files, sync sources, new candidates and conditional conversation file/image counts.
conditions: Image and PDF capabilities are looked up from model definitions; fallback differs by capability.
Conversation cap checks are feature-gated and may be disabled for certain hosts.

claims.title: Shared ingress
claims.finding: Picker, paste and drag-drop eventually call the upload handler with source metadata; picker clears input value after processing. Directory handling keeps native folders only where supported and otherwise flattens entries.

claims.title: Drop ownership
claims.finding: The newer file ingress carries a target snapshot; a folder-containing result from a changed target is discarded with an explicit chat-changed notice. Unresolved native folder paths are surfaced separately.
conditions: Observed mismatch guard in this selected adapter is specifically conditioned on a nonempty folders array; it is not proof that every plain-file ingress uses this exact guard.

claims.title: Long paste policy
claims.finding: The classic paste adapter uses a 4096 UTF-8-byte threshold; ordinary long text can become an attachment, while Shift, empty text, a disabling option or a short paste preserves editor insertion. Office-like HTML plus image clipboard data can prefer text.
conditions: Threshold belongs to the inspected paste adapter, not a universal service limit.
A paste can be promoted to a file by the injected attachPasteAsFile callback.

claims.title: Pasted content hygiene
claims.finding: The editor has a hidden-character paste extension with text/HTML transforms, VS Code clipboard handling, and removal of listeners when the editor view is destroyed.
conditions: Cleaning is gated in the extension; internal editor drags are distinguished from external paste/drop.

claims.title: Immediate staging
claims.finding: Placeholder mode attempts a bounded local inline-text fast path and otherwise creates local Blob records with UUID, filename, size, nativeFile and optional localPath before derivation resolves.
conditions: Fast path depends on target store and extension/size support.

claims.title: Handler chain
claims.finding: First matching handler wins. Registration order is unsupported guard, direct large-file route, size guard, PDF, image, document conversion, out-of-context files, text, and a final session file-store route.

claims.title: Batch scheduling and stable order
claims.finding: Matching and validation precede concurrent preprocessing. Process/upload execution is limited to four jobs; preprocessing results are stored by original index, and Promise.all preserves result order.
conditions: The four-slot limit applies to this processor; an outer upload pacing mechanism is separate.

claims.title: Batch refusal propagation
claims.finding: After a server refusal known to apply to the batch, remaining always-upload handlers are skipped. After the last successful process, eight failures lasting at least 540000 ms each can stop launching later uploads.
conditions: This is a guarded slow-failure breaker, not an overall nine-minute upload timeout.

claims.title: Local text decoding
claims.finding: Plain/code-like text can be decoded from arrayBuffer with encoding detection and fatal TextDecoder. An undecodable buffer produces an encoding-pending path; nontext binary detection samples up to 8000 bytes.

claims.title: Text normalization
claims.finding: Extracted text/file metadata have NUL characters removed. Upload filename normalization uses NFC with compatibility-ideograph exclusions. This is not language parsing or semantic code analysis.

claims.title: Byte-based inline budget
claims.finding: Inline attachment size is counted as UTF-8 bytes and memoized per object. A reservation ledger includes existing attachments and in-flight reservations to avoid concurrent over-admission; release is idempotent.
conditions: This is byte budgeting, not model tokenization.

claims.title: Inline-to-file promotion
claims.finding: Text that exceeds an individual or combined inline budget can be uploaded as a text/plain file when the active host permits files. Otherwise a specific single-item/aggregate error is returned.
conditions: Legacy branches without an out-of-context route can still return an inline attachment after the budget helper declines it; do not claim every path hard-blocks.

claims.title: PDF conversion boundary
claims.finding: PDF rasterization is requested when both the feature and model PDF capability are active. The fallbackToTextExtraction method calls server document conversion, not a local PDF parser.
unknowns: Server OCR/extraction layout algorithms and model-ready page encoding are not supplied by this client branch.

claims.title: Long and textless PDF branches
claims.finding: Conditional paths preserve an over-page-limit PDF as a whole file, retry as extracted text/text file, or request page images for a textless PDF. Client metadata distinguishes these outcomes.
conditions: These paths depend on document-as-file policy, long-PDF flags, route and server error codes.
The selected code does not declare one universal PDF page limit.

claims.title: Table and document routing
claims.finding: CSV is present in both text and out-of-context extension sets; XLS/XLSX have a conversion path when out-of-context files are disabled and size permits. Supported document formats route to conversion or whole-file storage according to policy.
conditions: Handler priority and current capabilities decide the route; extension alone is insufficient.
unknowns: No client evidence here establishes server spreadsheet formula evaluation, table flattening rules or preservation of styles.

claims.title: JPEG downscale parameters
claims.finding: Eligible non-project JPEG photos use a lazy local worker with a 2576-pixel long-edge target and 0.85 JPEG quality. Images within target keep original bytes; an output that is not smaller is discarded.
conditions: This photo path is conditional on JPEG matching and non-project use.
The bundled constants are upload preprocessing choices, not model vision-resolution limits.

claims.title: Worker safety and orientation
claims.finding: The JPEG worker path checks encoded dimensions, refuses >80000000 decoded pixels, requires bitmap/offscreen-canvas support, probes EXIF orientation, serializes work, and closes bitmaps. Queue timeout is 10000 ms; job timeout 15000 ms; repeated worker failure causes a 600000 ms cooldown.
conditions: Failure outcomes retain the original file; the upload pipeline may then apply its other image branch.

claims.title: General canvas and format conversion
claims.finding: The general image handler has a separate canvas resize branch capped at 8000 by 8000. BMP/HEIC/HEIF conversion uses JPEG; its helper default is 4096 and the eligible non-project HEIC path uses the photo long-edge target. The canvas helper revokes object URLs and removes the canvas.
conditions: Platform decode and smoothing support can force original-file fallback.
An 8000 cap is a client branch declaration, not a product-wide upload or context limit.

claims.title: Large-file two-stage upload
claims.finding: A higher-capability conversation-bound path can precede the ordinary 30 MiB guard. It first prepares a server filename/path and identity, then submits bytes to file storage, checks source/stored size agreement, and conditionally cleans up failed partial results.
conditions: Requires conversation identity and a higher configured upload cap.

After an upload result exists, empty stored output or changed source size enters deletion directly. Other failures delete only when a returned filename exists and the shared-path guard explicitly permits deletion; that guard is not universal across failure branches.
unknowns: Maximum account cap and server retention behavior are not established.

claims.title: Held derivation and rerouting
claims.finding: Derivation can wait for a send/ceiling hold or unresolved document-as-file policy. It races cancellation, rejects conversation changes, and aborts/restarts a document derivation when its policy changes.

claims.title: Retry taxonomy
claims.finding: Per-file processing retains hard error, soft error and sendBlocked states. A selected network-failure policy permits automatic retries after 1000 and 5000 ms; manual retry clears pending error state. Validation failures and intentional aborts follow separate paths.
conditions: The retry predicate requires online/not-unloading state, sufficient elapsed attempt time and a classified transport failure.
These delays are not a blanket policy for every upload or every server error.

claims.title: Preview and error rendering
claims.finding: Attachment tiles branch by image, Blob, sanitized document, session file and inline text. A native image can supply a preview before server preview_asset arrives; hard error or blocked files use a diagnostic tile.

claims.title: Removal ownership
claims.finding: Removing a file aborts its task, drops the staged record and records explicit user removal. Session-backed deletion checks other holders and same-path/same-name staged files before deciding whether to delete remote bytes.
conditions: Removing a tile is not proof that the remote object is deleted immediately.

claims.title: Draft persistence split
claims.finding: Draft persistence stores editor JSON, filtered attachments, stable file metadata, sync sources and queued/held drafts. Native File bytes are persisted separately; promises, AbortControllers and transient errors are stripped. Hydration stitches blobs back and can mark an unrecoverable reference unavailable.
conditions: Persistence is disabled/suppressed in selected new-chat, temporary, session-mismatch and URL-seeded contexts.

claims.title: Hydration and cleanup
claims.finding: Hydration tracks text readiness separately from attachment-blob readiness, can retain temporary text/attachment placeholders, and folds restored queued input around the draft in defined order. Cleanup flushes pending pastes/writes and uses ownership-aware delayed blob release.

claims.title: Navigation handover
claims.finding: A selected new-composer handover uses an in-memory snapshot with account, draft key and a 5000 ms freshness window; teardown aborts pending file tasks unless the store still owns a held, awaiting-acceptance or active send.
conditions: This is a narrow handover branch, not a universal draft-retention timeout.

claims.title: Dictation ownership and capability
claims.finding: Dictation state has owner identity, status, final/interim transcripts, microphone state, drain state and failure details. Capability combines platform support, desktop-provided availability or web feature flags, surface and responsive conditions.

claims.title: Dictation lifecycle
claims.finding: The composer-owned dictation adapter stops on busy state, gate removal, hiding, unmount, conversation change or draft generation change. Enter normally commits; Escape cancels; a held shortcut switches to push-to-talk after 500 ms. Transcript reconciliation preserves prefix/suffix and can preserve edits made while recording.
conditions: Enter passthrough exists in a separate host configuration.
Full voice conversation is a separate state machine from short dictation.

claims.title: Voice navigation handoff
claims.finding: An active full-voice session can hand off the retained interim transcript at the navigation-ready transition, updated by eligible non-empty interim changes, to a newly created conversation with an explicit user-message identity; the effect unsubscribes and clears handed-off interim text on cleanup.

claims.title: Ordering is route-specific
claims.finding: The selected session message builder emits images before text in its ordinary branch; recording-frame mode interleaves frame-related text with images. Draft queue restoration uses before-draft and after-draft groups. Queued files are filtered against UUIDs already in the current draft; the helper does not globally deduplicate UUIDs across different queued entries. Sync-source identifiers are deduplicated across the merged collection.
unknowns: These client array orders do not reveal final server system/tool/project/history prompt ordering.

claims.title: Estimates versus token accounting
claims.finding: Project knowledge has a byte/4 heuristic. A separate coding-session attribution helper estimates text with ceil(length/4) and uses 1600 for image/document blocks. Neither is verified as the main chat model tokenizer.
conditions: The latter appears in attribution/usage processing, not attachment admission.

claims.title: Cache observation boundary
claims.finding: Coding-session accounting consumes cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens; another client view derives a context total and cache age from reported usage/timestamps. This demonstrates observation, not cache-placement control.
unknowns: No placement, TTL, hit eligibility, server cache key, or model prompt prefix policy is established by these counters.

claims.title: Local preview resource ownership
claims.finding: Native image previews share an object URL per File with a subscriber set; removing the final subscriber revokes the URL and removes the cache entry.

negative_scope.searched_in: All 3426 assets/v1 JavaScript files in packaged ion-dist
negative_scope.interpretation: Literal absence is only a bounded search result, not proof that no cache or estimation implementation exists.

reproduction_policy: Publish original explanations, diagrams and compact anchors only; do not distribute extracted bundles or raw REA graphs.

source_evidence.observed_control_flow: p is an UploadStoredEmptyError check; kk is UploadSourceChangedError. Either sets m true.
With a prepared upload u, m alone chooses the deleted branch. isUploadPathShared is consulted only by the alternate named-upload branch; JavaScript || short-circuits before that guard when m is true.
The sharing helper is conservative when the callback is absent or throws, but that does not make it run for the two integrity-error cases.

The Set is initialized only from current draft files. The queue helper filters with !l.has(file_uuid), but never adds accepted queued UUIDs. Before- and after-draft queue groups are filtered separately against the same unchanged Set.
The no-savings outcome applies to an output whose size is greater than or equal to the input size.
Each changed, non-empty interim transcript updates the retained value while the eligibility condition holds.
The navigation-ready handoff uses that retained value, which can be the latest of several interim updates.
